title: AI Debt Spree Hammers Tech Debt as Traders Rush to Reprice Risk
source_used: Bloomberg (text read on Yahoo Finance UK)
key_facts: Bloomberg reports that heavyweights including Oracle, Broadcom and SpaceX priced nearly half a trillion dollars of new debt this year to pay for AI infrastructure.

Credit default swaps (contracts that pay out if a borrower fails to repay) linked to hyperscalers and chipmakers have risen to prices that suggest traders see a growing risk of default over five years: above 20% for Oracle, about 16% for SpaceX and more than 7% for Nvidia.
Oracle's five-year credit insurance rose about 10.5 basis points on Thursday to a record close of 261 basis points; Broadcom's widened 3 basis points to a record 136.
There have been nine US high-grade bond deals of $25 billion or more this year, the most ever, mostly in tech.
Broadcom launched a $60 billion debt financing to help fund Anthropic's AI buildout, and may raise about $600 billion in coming years by Bloomberg's own calculation.
The Wall Street Journal reported Oracle is in talks with Apollo and Goldman Sachs about financing a big chip purchase; SpaceX is reported to be seeking $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips.
Investors are demanding more compensation to lend to the sector, according to fixed-income portfolio manager Steven Kohlenstein.
quote_evidence: Some days it feels like the market is holding an emergency meeting every few hours to reprice the size of the AI buildout.
why_it_matters_hint: Lenders are asking more to finance the AI buildout, which raises the cost of the borrowing that pays for it.
